custom-chin-implant-silicone-medpor.text: Users consider a chin implant to add projection, and sometimes height or width, to a recessed chin, as a less invasive route than sliding genioplasty. The change in profile is visible once healed. Silicone, porous polyethylene and patient-specific designs are discussed, with outcomes documented mainly in surgical case series.

chin-filler.text: Chin filler, often called a liquid genioplasty, is used to add projection or length to the chin without surgery, and the change in profile is visible right after treatment. People use it to preview or approximate surgical results. Hyaluronic acid fillers are studied for chin augmentation, with effects that are temporary.

vertical-chin-lengthening.text: Vertical chin lengthening is discussed by people with a short lower third of the face who want a taller chin rather than a more forward one. The height change is visible once healed. The surgical literature on genioplasty with grafts or implants consists mostly of small case series.

chin-reduction-shaving.text: Chin reduction is discussed by people whose chin looks too large or prominent and who want a smaller, better-proportioned lower face. The reduction in size is visible once healed. Techniques include burring the bone and osteotomy with setback, described in surgical papers.

double-jaw-surgery-for-retrognathia.text: Double-jaw surgery is the major structural option discussed for a recessed lower jaw, moving the mandible and upper jaw forward together to improve both bite and profile. The skeletal change is visible and measurable after healing. It is a well-established orthognathic operation with an extensive surgical literature.

chain: Line drawn nose tip to chin
Profile goals for chin and lips
profile-analysis-ricketts-e-line.text: Forum users apply the E-line to side-profile photos to judge where the lips sit relative to the nose and chin, and to decide whether chin or lip changes are of interest. It is a standard orthodontic reference measurement. Preferred lip positions vary between observers and over time.

chain: Lower jaw grows or shifts forward
orthodontic-functional-appliances-herbst.text: Users interested in profile improvement discuss Herbst and Twin Block appliances for growing teens with a recessed lower jaw and overbite. They are studied in randomized trials in adolescents, where how much change is jaw growth versus tooth movement is debated. Use in adults for facial appearance rests on anecdote.

chain: Chin and neck line up better
neck-posture-forward-head-correction.text: Forum posters promote correcting forward head posture to sharpen the jawline and profile, since the head sits further over the shoulders when upright. Posture correction is well studied for neck pain, but its effect on how the chin and jaw look has not been tested.

jaw-advancement-for-sleep-apnea-mad-devi.text: Mandibular advancement devices are a sleep-apnea mouthpiece, and some forum users wonder whether wearing one could also shift the lower jaw forward for a better profile. They are well studied for snoring and breathing during sleep, while any facial-appearance effect is untested.

fat-grafting-to-chin.text: Fat grafting is discussed as a way to build out a small chin using the person's own fat, as an alternative to implants, genioplasty or fillers. The added volume is visible after treatment. Fat grafting is an established technique in general, with limited chin-specific data, and some of the fat can be reabsorbed.

weight-loss-for-chin-definition.text: Users lose body fat to reduce submental fullness and show the chin and jawline more clearly, mainly where a double chin is soft tissue. It changes the covering fat rather than bone structure. No studies test fat loss specifically for chin definition.

submalar-filler.text: Submalar filler is used to add volume in the hollow beneath the cheekbone, as a non-surgical counterpart to submalar implants. The change in cheek contour is visible after treatment and is temporary. Evidence in the sources reviewed consists of small registered trials.

malar-augmentation-with-fat-grafting.text: People use fat grafting to add volume and projection over the cheekbones with their own tissue, as an alternative to implants or hyaluronic acid fillers. The added fullness is visible after treatment. Fat grafting is widely used in the face, though cheek-specific evidence is thin and some fat can be reabsorbed.

zygomatic-arch-reduction-reduction-malar.text: Reduction malarplasty is used to narrow wide or prominent cheekbones, and is among the more commonly requested facial-contour procedures in East Asia. The narrower face is visible after healing. Support comes mainly from surgeon case series.

cheekbone-makeup-contour-highlight.text: Users apply darker shades beneath the cheekbone and lighter or shimmering shades on top to make cheekbones look more defined for photos or an evening. The effect is visible immediately and washes off. It is a cosmetic technique with no clinical research behind it.

chain: Fuller cheek, less hollow lower lid
midface-lift.text: A midface lift repositions sagging cheek and lower-eyelid tissue upward to restore a fuller, younger cheek and soften a hollowed lower lid. The lift is visible once healed. It is described as suited to people in their 40s without marked jowling, with evidence mostly from surgeon case series.

maxilla-expansion-for-forward-growth-fac.text: Forum users discuss reverse-pull headgear, or face pulling, as a way to bring the upper jaw and midface forward for a better profile. It is studied in children with underbites and a retrusive maxilla. Its use as an appearance tool in adults is based on anecdote.

facial-thread-lift-cheek-lifting.text: Thread lifts are used as a minimally invasive way to raise the midface and soften the nasolabial fold without removing skin. The lift is visible after the procedure. Efficacy data are limited and mixed, with complications reported in the literature.

cheek-fat-pad-bichat-removal.text: Buccal fat removal is popular in looksmaxxing communities as a route to hollow cheeks and a more visible cheekbone-to-jaw transition, often tied to the ogee curve. The slimmer lower cheek is visible after healing. Published outcome data are limited.

hollow-cheeks-via-chewing-then-fat-loss.text: Forum posters combine masseter-focused chewing with fat loss to bring out cheekbones and jaw structure and create hollow cheeks. They describe hollowness as coming from bone and muscle, revealed by less soft tissue. No studies test the combination.

frontal-orbital-advancement-frontal-boss.text: In looksmaxxing usage, frontal-orbital advancement refers to surgery meant to push the brow ridge and upper orbital area forward for a more prominent brow and deeper-set eyes. The sources reviewed cover brow lifts and brow reduction rather than cosmetic advancement, so this specific goal is largely untested.

ogee-curve-analysis.text: The ogee curve is the S-shaped line from the cheekbone into the cheek hollow, used in aesthetic surgery as a filler goal and promoted online as a beauty marker. Forum users assess it in front and three-quarter photos to guide cheek treatments. Claims about it separating attractive from average faces are anecdotal.

chain: Lower lid sits tighter and higher
canthopexy.text: Canthopexy tightens and repositions the lower eyelid without cutting the outer corner, and forum users discuss it for a firmer lid line and almond or fox-eye shape. The change is visible once healed. It is a routine companion to lower blepharoplasty, while its use for eye shape is untested.

chain: Lower lid anchored to orbital rim
tarsal-strip-procedure.text: Forum users discuss the tarsal strip for tightening a lax lower eyelid and reducing sagging or visible white below the iris. The tighter lid is visible after healing. It is an established oculoplastic operation, with evidence mostly about lid function rather than cosmetic outcomes.

chain: Eye opens at the inner corner
medial-epicanthoplasty.text: Medial epicanthoplasty removes or reduces the epicanthal fold over the inner eye corner to open up the eye, and is often paired with double eyelid surgery. The change is visible once healed. It is well described in the Asian blepharoplasty literature, mostly as case series.

double-eyelid-surgery-asian-blepharoplas.text: Double eyelid surgery forms an upper-lid crease for people who lack one, and is among the most commonly performed cosmetic procedures in East Asia. The crease and more open eye are visible after healing. The literature is large, though mostly case series rather than controlled trials.

chain: Upper lid folds at the crease
non-incisional-double-eyelid-suture-meth.text: The suture method creates an upper-lid crease with buried stitches instead of an incision, and is popular in Asia, especially China. The crease is visible soon after the procedure. The literature focuses on how long the crease lasts and on suture complications.

ptosis-surgery-levator-advancement.text: Ptosis repair raises a drooping upper eyelid, and forum users discuss the more open, more alert eye it produces. The lifted lid is visible after healing. It is primarily a functional operation supported by medical case series, with appearance benefit discussed mainly by patients.

chain: Eyes look more open and awake
oxymetazoline-eye-drops-upneeq.text: Upneeq is a prescription oxymetazoline eye drop approved for acquired ptosis, used for a temporary lift of the upper lid that makes eyes look more open. Forum users also discuss nasal-spray substitutes, which are not the approved product. The lid lift is studied in ptosis trials.

chain: Double eyelid or more open eye
eyelid-tape-fold-stickers.text: Eyelid tape and fold stickers create a temporary upper-lid crease, and many East Asian users wear them for a double eyelid look or to open hooded eyes. The effect is visible immediately and removable. It is the non-surgical counterpart to double eyelid surgery.
